kap.t: Chapter 1: Programs and the Python Interpreter
a: From source code to execution: compiler and interpreter
Controlling loops, nesting them and collecting results
Solutions by trying: guess and check, approximation with a tolerance
Application: the interest rate of an installment loan

karten.v: program
karten.r: A program is a sequence of unambiguously described steps that a computer carries out one after another, without asking questions.

karten.v: statement
karten.r: A single step of a program is called a statement.

karten.v: processor
karten.r: In a computer, the steps of a program are carried out by the processor, a chip that calculates and controls the sequence of steps.

karten.v: machine instruction
karten.r: A machine instruction is an instruction that the processor can carry out directly.

karten.v: machine code
karten.r: A program that consists only of machine instructions is called machine code.

karten.v: programming language
karten.r: A programming language is an artificial language in which it is precisely defined which texts are allowed and what each allowed text does.

karten.v: syntax
karten.r: The syntax of a programming language is the set of all rules that determine which texts are allowed in it.

karten.v: semantics
karten.r: The semantics of a programming language determines what an allowed text means, that is, what happens when it is run.

karten.v: source code
karten.r: The source code of a program is its text in a programming language, the way people write and read it.

karten.v: A ______ is a recipe of unambiguous steps that a computer can carry out without asking back.
karten.r: A program is a recipe of unambiguous steps that a computer can carry out without asking back.

karten.v: The ______ understands only very simple machine instructions, which are stored as numbers in memory, and each processor family has its own.
karten.r: The processor understands only very simple machine instructions, which are stored as numbers in memory, and each processor family has its own.

karten.v: A ______ is an artificial language without ambiguity in which programs are written down.
karten.r: A programming language is an artificial language without ambiguity in which programs are written down.

karten.v: The ______ determines the allowed form, regardless of what a text means.
karten.r: The syntax determines the allowed form, regardless of what a text means.

karten.v: The ______ determines what an allowed text does.
karten.r: The semantics determines what an allowed text does.

karten.v: ______ is the program in the form in which people write it; the processor cannot run it directly.
karten.r: Source code is the program in the form in which people write it; the processor cannot run it directly.

karten.v: compiler
karten.r: A compiler is a program that translates a source code completely into machine code before that code is run.

karten.v: executable file
karten.r: Such a file is called an executable file.

karten.v: interpreter
karten.r: An interpreter is a program that reads a source code and itself carries out the steps described in it.

karten.v: Python
karten.r: Python is a programming language; its syntax and semantics are laid down in the Python Language Reference.

karten.v: CPython
karten.r: CPython is the program that runs Python source code and is offered on python.org; it is itself written in the C language.

karten.v: Bytecode
karten.r: Bytecode is a sequence of simple instructions into which CPython translates the entire source code before it begins running it.

karten.v: interpreter loop
karten.r: A part of CPython then works through the bytecode instruction by instruction: the interpreter loop.

karten.v: A ______ translates the whole source code once, in advance, into an executable file of machine code.
karten.r: A compiler translates the whole source code once, in advance, into an executable file of machine code.

karten.v: An ______ runs the source code itself, without producing an executable file.
karten.r: An interpreter runs the source code itself, without producing an executable file.

karten.v: ______ is the language; CPython is the program that runs it.
karten.r: Python is the language; CPython is the program that runs it.

karten.v: ______ first translates the whole file into bytecode and then runs this bytecode instruction by instruction.
karten.r: CPython first translates the whole file into bytecode and then runs this bytecode instruction by instruction.

karten.v: Python install manager
karten.r: The Python install manager is a program for Windows that downloads, installs, lists, removes and starts Python versions.

karten.v: version number
karten.r: A Python version number has the form 3.14.4 and consists of three parts.

karten.v: On Windows, you install the ______ and then start Python with py.
karten.r: On Windows, you install the Python install manager and then start Python with py.

karten.v: On Linux, ______ is usually already there and is called python3.
karten.r: On Linux, Python is usually already there and is called python3.

karten.v: The ______ tells you which Python you have; version numbers are compared part by part.
karten.r: The version number tells you which Python you have; version numbers are compared part by part.

karten.v: interactive mode
karten.r: In interactive mode, Python reads an input, runs it, displays the result and then waits for the next input.

karten.v: value
karten.r: A value is a single piece of data that Python works with, for example the number 42 or the number 0.5.

karten.v: expression
karten.r: An expression is a piece of source code that Python can compute to a value.

karten.v: evaluation
karten.r: Computing the value of an expression is called evaluation.

karten.v: string
karten.r: A string is a value that consists of text.

karten.v: function
karten.r: A function is a ready-made subprogram with a name that you can have run when needed.

karten.v: function call
karten.r: A function call has a function run.

karten.v: In ______, you type a line after >>>, and Python answers immediately.
karten.r: In interactive mode, you type a line after >>>, and Python answers immediately.

karten.v: A ______ is a piece of data such as the number 42; in Python, decimal places come after a point.
karten.r: A value is a piece of data such as the number 42; in Python, decimal places come after a point.

karten.v: An ______ is source code that yields a value; the interactive mode displays this value immediately.
karten.r: An expression is source code that yields a value; the interactive mode displays this value immediately.

karten.v: ______ calculates with + - * / ** and round parentheses according to the rules of mathematics; decimal places come after a point, and it knows no units.
karten.r: Python calculates with + - * / ** and round parentheses according to the rules of mathematics; decimal places come after a point, and it knows no units.

karten.v: Heron's recipe runs in ______ pass by pass and, after five passes, arrives at the built-in result of 2 ** 0.5 except for the last digit.
karten.r: Heron's recipe runs in interactive mode pass by pass and, after five passes, arrives at the built-in result of 2 ** 0.5 except for the last digit.

karten.v: Text in straight quotation marks is a ______, that is, a value that Python does not calculate with.
karten.r: Text in straight quotation marks is a string, that is, a value that Python does not calculate with.

karten.v: A ______ is a ready-made subprogram with a name.
karten.r: A function is a ready-made subprogram with a name.

karten.v: You call a ______ with its name and round parentheses; print writes the values in the parentheses to the terminal.
karten.r: You call a function with its name and round parentheses; print writes the values in the parentheses to the terminal.

karten.v: editor
karten.r: An editor is a program with which you write and save plain text files.

karten.v: script
karten.r: A script is a text file with Python source code whose name ends in .py.

karten.v: comment
karten.r: A comment begins with the character # and extends to the end of the line.

karten.v: You write ______ with an editor that saves plain text, ideally with an editor for programmers such as VS Code or IDLE.
karten.r: You write programs with an editor that saves plain text, ideally with an editor for programmers such as VS Code or IDLE.

karten.v: A ______ is a .py file that you run with py datei.py or python3 datei.py; only what print outputs becomes visible in it.
karten.r: A script is a .py file that you run with py datei.py or python3 datei.py; only what print outputs becomes visible in it.

karten.v: A ______ begins with #, applies up to the end of the line and is there only for humans.
karten.r: A comment begins with #, applies up to the end of the line and is there only for humans.

karten.v: syntax error
karten.r: A syntax error is a place in the source code that violates the syntax of the language.

karten.v: runtime error
karten.r: A runtime error is an error that occurs only when a line is run.

karten.v: exception
karten.r: An exception is the event with which Python reports an error.

karten.v: traceback
karten.r: The traceback is the report that Python outputs when an exception aborts a program while it is running.

karten.v: logic error
karten.r: A logic error is an error in which a program runs without an error message but does not compute what was intended.

karten.v: A ______ violates the form; Python reports it before the start, and no line of the file runs.
karten.r: A syntax error violates the form; Python reports it before the start, and no line of the file runs.

karten.v: A ______ occurs when a line is run; everything before it has run, nothing after it has.
karten.r: A runtime error occurs when a line is run; everything before it has run, nothing after it has.

karten.v: An ______ reports an error with a type and a description; while the program is running, it aborts the program.
karten.r: An exception reports an error with a type and a description; while the program is running, it aborts the program.

karten.v: A ______ names the location and the type of an exception; you read it from the bottom.
karten.r: A traceback names the location and the type of an exception; you read it from the bottom.

karten.v: A ______ runs without a message and yields a wrong result; you find it only by checking results.
karten.r: A logic error runs without a message and yields a wrong result; you find it only by checking results.

karten.v: object
karten.r: An object is a piece of main memory in which Python stores a value, together with the information about what kind of value is stored there.

karten.v: type
karten.r: The type of an object is the kind of its value.

karten.v: identity
karten.r: The identity of an object is an integer that distinguishes the object from all other objects that exist at the same time.

karten.v: method
karten.r: A method is a function that belongs to a type.

karten.v: An ______ is a value in main memory that carries the information about its kind with it.
karten.r: An object is a value in main memory that carries the information about its kind with it.

karten.v: The ______ says what kind of value an object contains and what you can do with it; type displays it.
karten.r: The type says what kind of value an object contains and what you can do with it; type displays it.

karten.v: The ______ is the fixed number of an object; id displays it.
karten.r: The identity is the fixed number of an object; id displays it.

karten.v: A ______ is a function of a type; you call it with objekt.name().
karten.r: A method is a function of a type; you call it with objekt.name().

karten.v: operator
karten.r: An operator is a symbol that computes a new value from values.

karten.v: operands
karten.r: The values an operator acts on are called its operands.

karten.v: floor division, remainder
karten.r: The operator // is called floor division; the operator % returns the remainder.

karten.v: precedence
karten.r: The precedence of the operators determines which operator in an expression without parentheses is carried out first.

karten.v: Theorem 2.5 (Floor division and remainder)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{a }\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{ (a\,/\!/\,b)\cdot b + a\,\%\,b .}$$

karten.v: An int is an integer of arbitrary size; ______ calculates with it exactly.
karten.r: An int is an integer of arbitrary size; Python calculates with it exactly.

karten.v: An ______ computes a new value from its operands; if one operand is a float, so is the result.
karten.r: An operator computes a new value from its operands; if one operand is a float, so is the result.

karten.v: // rounds the quotient down, toward $-\infty$; % is the matching ______ and has the sign of the right operand.
karten.r: // rounds the quotient down, toward $-\infty$; % is the matching remainder and has the sign of the right operand.

karten.v: ** binds more tightly than a minus sign in front of it and is evaluated from right to left; a negative ______ returns a float.
karten.r: ** binds more tightly than a minus sign in front of it and is evaluated from right to left; a negative exponent returns a float.

karten.v: base
karten.r: Let $B\ge2$ be a natural number, the base.

karten.v: binary number
karten.r: A binary number is a number in the positional numeral system with base $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{B}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2}$.

karten.v: bit
karten.r: A digit of a binary number is called a bit, short for binary digit.

karten.v: byte
karten.r: A byte is a group of 8 bits.

karten.v: hexadecimal number
karten.r: A hexadecimal number is a number in the positional numeral system with base $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{B}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{16}$.

karten.v: binary fraction
karten.r: A binary fraction is a number in the binary system with digits to the right of the point, the binary point.

karten.v: doubling method
karten.r: For $0\le x<1$, the doubling method determines the binary digits of $x$: you double $x$.

karten.v: Definition 3.1 (Positional numeral system)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{z_{n-1}B^{n-1}+\dots+z_1B^1+z_0B^0}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}z_i\,B^i .}$$

karten.v: Definition 3.5 (Binary fraction)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{0.b_{-1}b_{-2}\ldots b_{-m}\,{}_2}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\sum_{k=1}^{m}b_{-k}\,2^{-k} .}$$

karten.v: In a positional numeral system, each digit is multiplied by the place ______ of its position, and everything is added up.
karten.r: In a positional numeral system, each digit is multiplied by the place value of its position, and everything is added up.

karten.v: A ______ has only the digits 0 and 1, the bits; each bit counts $2^i$.
karten.r: A binary number has only the digits 0 and 1, the bits; each bit counts $2^i$.

karten.v: A ______ is 8 bits; it can take 256 different values, the numbers 0 to 255.
karten.r: A byte is 8 bits; it can take 256 different values, the numbers 0 to 255.

karten.v: Repeated division by 2 yields the bits as ______, the last bit first; ready-made, bin and format do the job.
karten.r: Repeated division by 2 yields the bits as remainders, the last bit first; ready-made, bin and format do the job.

karten.v: Hexadecimal is ______ 16; each digit stands for four bits, a byte for two digits.
karten.r: Hexadecimal is base 16; each digit stands for four bits, a byte for two digits.

karten.v: A ______ terminates exactly when the denominator in lowest terms is a power of two; $0.1$ does not terminate.
karten.r: A binary fraction terminates exactly when the denominator in lowest terms is a power of two; $0.1$ does not terminate.

karten.v: floating-point number
karten.r: A floating-point number with $p$ binary digits is a number of the form $\pm\,m\cdot2^E$.

karten.v: exponent
karten.r: The exponent $E$ is an integer from a fixed range.

karten.v: exponent field
karten.r: The exponent field $c$ of a float stores the exponent shifted by 1023.

karten.v: significand field
karten.r: The significand field $t$ of a float contains the 52 binary digits of the significand after the point.

karten.v: representation error
karten.r: If $x$ lies exactly halfway between two float values, Python takes the one whose last significand bit is 0. The difference between the stored value and $x$ is called the representation error.

karten.v: Definition 4.3 (Exponent field)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{c}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{E+1023,\qquad E}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{c-1023 .}$$

karten.v: Definition 4.4 (Significand field)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{m}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1+\frac{t}{2^{52}} .}$$

karten.v: The significand field
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{x}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{(-1)^s\cdot\Bigl(1+\frac{t}{2^{52}}\Bigr)\cdot2^{\,c-1023}.}$$

karten.v: A ______ is a significand times a power of two; with a fixed number of digits, the spacing of neighboring numbers grows with their magnitude.
karten.r: A floating-point number is a significand times a power of two; with a fixed number of digits, the spacing of neighboring numbers grows with their magnitude.

karten.v: A float is a ______ with a significand of 53 binary digits, stored in 64 bits: sign, exponent field, significand field.
karten.r: A float is a floating-point number with a significand of 53 binary digits, stored in 64 bits: sign, exponent field, significand field.

karten.v: The ______ stores $E+1023$; this way, it does without a sign.
karten.r: The exponent field stores $E+1023$; this way, it does without a sign.

karten.v: The ______ stores the 52 digits after the point; you add the leading 1 when reading it.
karten.r: The significand field stores the 52 digits after the point; you add the leading 1 when reading it.

karten.v: hex shows a float as $\pm$0x1.______pexponent.
karten.r: hex shows a float as $\pm$0x1.significand fieldpexponent.

karten.v: ______ stores the nearest float; for 0.1, that is $\frac{3602879701896397}{2^{55}}$, too large by about $5.6\cdot10^{-18}$.
karten.r: Python stores the nearest float; for 0.1, that is $\frac{3602879701896397}{2^{55}}$, too large by about $5.6\cdot10^{-18}$.

karten.v: rounding error
karten.r: The difference that arises is called the rounding error of the calculation.

karten.v: Machine epsilon
karten.r: Machine epsilon $\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}$ is the distance from 1 to the next larger float.

karten.v: absorbed
karten.r: If $|b|$ is smaller than half the spacing of the float values near $a$, then $a+b$ gives $a$ again: the small summand is lost completely. It is said to be absorbed.

karten.v: Cancellation
karten.r: Cancellation is the loss of significant digits when you subtract two almost equal numbers that already carry rounding errors.

karten.v: overflow
karten.r: If the rounded result of a calculation is larger, this is called overflow, and the result is the special value inf (infinity), for negative results -inf.

karten.v: Definition 5.2 (Machine epsilon)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2^{-52}}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2.22\cdot10^{-16}.}$$

karten.v: Theorem 5.3 (Size of the rounding error)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{|\tilde x-x|\le\frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm M}}{2}\,|x|}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{2^{-53}\,|x|}\textcolor{#15633a}{\approx}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1.11\cdot10^{-16}\,|x| .}$$

karten.v: A summand that is smaller than half the spacing of the float ______ near the other summand disappears in the addition.
karten.r: A summand that is smaller than half the spacing of the float values near the other summand disappears in the addition.

karten.v: Results above $1.797\cdot10^{308}$ become inf; ______ continues to calculate with inf as with $\infty$, only ** raises an OverflowError.
karten.r: Results above $1.797\cdot10^{308}$ become inf; Python continues to calculate with inf as with $\infty$, only ** raises an OverflowError.

karten.v: variable
karten.r: A name that is bound to an object is called a variable.

karten.v: augmented assignment
karten.r: For an arithmetic operator $\circ$ from + - * / // % **, the augmented assignment name $\circ$= expression means the same for numbers as name = name $\circ$ (expression).

karten.v: name = ausdruck evaluates the ______ and binds the name to the result.
karten.r: name = ausdruck evaluates the expression and binds the name to the result.

karten.v: A ______ is a name that is bound to an object; it comes into being with the first assignment.
karten.r: A variable is a name that is bound to an object; it comes into being with the first assignment.

karten.v: An ______ attaches a tag to an object or moves the tag to another object; it copies nothing.
karten.r: An assignment attaches a tag to an object or moves the tag to another object; it copies nothing.

karten.v: ______ turn fixed numbers into named assumptions; the formulas below them calculate with the names.
karten.r: Variables turn fixed numbers into named assumptions; the formulas below them calculate with the names.

karten.v: comparison operators
karten.r: The comparison operators compare two values and return a bool.

karten.v: Definition 7.4 (Comparison with a relative tolerance)
karten.r: $$|a-b|\le r\cdot\max(|a|,|b|) .$$

karten.v: bool has the ______ True and False; in calculations, they count as 1 and 0.
karten.r: bool has the values True and False; in calculations, they count as 1 and 0.

karten.v: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= compare two ______ and return True or False.
karten.r: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= compare two values and return True or False.

karten.v: You compare ______ with a relative tolerance, $|a-b|\le r\max(|a|,|b|)$; near 0, you additionally need an absolute tolerance.
karten.r: You compare floating-point numbers with a relative tolerance, $|a-b|\le r\max(|a|,|b|)$; near 0, you additionally need an absolute tolerance.

karten.v: is asks whether two names mean the same ______; == asks whether two values are equal.
karten.r: is asks whether two names mean the same object; == asks whether two values are equal.

karten.v: None means “no ______”; you test for it with is None.
karten.r: None means “no value”; you test for it with is None.

karten.v: module
karten.r: A module is a file with ready-made Python definitions, such as functions and values.

karten.v: import modul loads a ______ and binds its name; modul.name accesses its contents.
karten.r: import modul loads a module and binds its name; modul.name accesses its contents.

karten.v: math contains the calculator ______ for float; angles are given in radians.
karten.r: math contains the calculator functions for float; angles are given in radians.

karten.v: sys.float_info describes the ______ float, math.ulp the spacing of neighboring float values; both confirm the calculations by hand.
karten.r: sys.float_info describes the type float, math.ulp the spacing of neighboring float values; both confirm the calculations by hand.

karten.v: attribute
karten.r: An attribute is a name that is attached to an object and accessed with a dot: object.name.

karten.v: complex stores the real and imaginary parts as two float ______; the imaginary unit is written 1j.
karten.r: complex stores the real and imaginary parts as two float values; the imaginary unit is written 1j.

karten.v: An ______ is a name attached to an object; z.real and z.imag return the real and imaginary parts.
karten.r: An attribute is a name attached to an object; z.real and z.imag return the real and imaginary parts.

karten.v: The absolute ______ by hand with Pythagoras, the phase with math.atan2(y, x); ready-made with abs, cmath.phase and cmath.polar.
karten.r: The absolute value by hand with Pythagoras, the phase with math.atan2(y, x); ready-made with abs, cmath.phase and cmath.polar.

karten.v: concatenation
karten.r: For strings, + means joining end to end, called concatenation: "Regen" + "schirm" is "Regenschirm" (German for “umbrella”).

karten.v: f-string
karten.r: An f-string is a string with an f before the opening quotation mark.

karten.v: type conversion
karten.r: The functions int, float and str create a new object from a value, with the type of their name. This is called type conversion.

karten.v: For ______, + concatenates, * repeats, and len counts the characters.
karten.r: For strings, + concatenates, * repeats, and len counts the characters.

karten.v: An ______ inserts the values in {...} into a text; after the colon, a format specifier determines the digits and the form.
karten.r: An f-string inserts the values in {...} into a text; after the colon, a format specifier determines the digits and the form.

karten.v: float(input(...)) reads a number, and an ______ outputs the result with a suitable number of digits.
karten.r: float(input(...)) reads a number, and an f-string outputs the result with a suitable number of digits.

karten.v: chained comparison
karten.r: If several comparison operators stand one after another, such as a < b <= c, the expression is called a chained comparison.

karten.v: short-circuit evaluation
karten.r: In a and b, b is evaluated only if a is true; in a or b, only if a is false. This rule is called short-circuit evaluation.

karten.v: truth value
karten.r: Every object has a truth value, True or False; the type conversion bool(x) shows it.

karten.v: A comparison is an ______ whose value is True or False.
karten.r: A comparison is an expression whose value is True or False.

karten.v: ______ compares strings character by character by their numbers; "10" < "9" is true, so convert inputs first, then compare.
karten.r: Python compares strings character by character by their numbers; "10" < "9" is true, so convert inputs first, then compare.

karten.v: Of the ______ known so far, zero, None, False and the empty string count as false, and all others as true.
karten.r: Of the values known so far, zero, None, False and the empty string count as false, and all others as true.

karten.v: and and or return one of their ______; wert or ersatz replaces every false value, even a genuine zero.
karten.r: and and or return one of their operands; wert or ersatz replaces every false value, even a genuine zero.

karten.v: header line
karten.r: The first line is called the header line; it begins with if and ends with a colon.

karten.v: block
karten.r: A block is a sequence of statements that are all indented by the same amount and follow a header line, that is, a line with a colon at the end.

karten.v: The indentation determines which lines belong to a ______; a block ends where a line starts further to the left again.
karten.r: The indentation determines which lines belong to a header line; a block ends where a line starts further to the left again.

karten.v: else specifies the ______ that runs if the condition is false.
karten.r: else specifies the block that runs if the condition is false.

karten.v: With if, elif and else, exactly the ______ of the first true condition runs, otherwise the else block.
karten.r: With if, elif and else, exactly the block of the first true condition runs, otherwise the else block.

karten.v: == instead of =, a colon at the end, every partial condition written out in full, ______ with a tolerance, inputs converted first.
karten.r: == instead of =, a colon at the end, every partial condition written out in full, floating-point numbers with a tolerance, inputs converted first.

karten.v: loop
karten.r: A statement that repeats a block is called a loop.

karten.v: iteration
karten.r: A single execution of the block is called an iteration.

karten.v: infinite loop
karten.r: An infinite loop is a loop whose condition never becomes false.

karten.v: while Bedingung: repeats the ______ as long as the condition is true before the iteration.
karten.r: while Bedingung: repeats the block as long as the condition is true before the iteration.

karten.v: If the ______ changes nothing the condition depends on, the loop runs forever; Ctrl+C interrupts it with KeyboardInterrupt.
karten.r: If the block changes nothing the condition depends on, the loop runs forever; Ctrl+C interrupts it with KeyboardInterrupt.

karten.v: Never let a ______ wait for a float with != or ==; count with integers and calculate the float from the counter.
karten.r: Never let a loop wait for a float with != or ==; count with integers and calculate the float from the counter.

karten.v: while is the right ______ when you do not know the number of iterations beforehand, only the goal.
karten.r: while is the right loop when you do not know the number of iterations beforehand, only the goal.

karten.v: loop variable
karten.r: The name is called the loop variable.

karten.v: Definition 4.2 (range)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{\mathtt{len}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\max\Bigl(0,\Bigl\lceil\frac{\mathtt{stop}-\mathtt{start}}{\mathtt{schritt}}\Bigr\rceil\Bigr).}$$

karten.v: for k in range(n): executes the ______ for $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{k}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0,1,\ldots,n-1}$.
karten.r: for k in range(n): executes the block for $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{k}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0,1,\ldots,n-1}$.

karten.v: For steps with ______, range counts with integers, and you calculate the value from the counter.
karten.r: For steps with floating-point numbers, range counts with integers, and you calculate the value from the counter.

karten.v: for when the sequence of ______ is known beforehand; while when only the goal is known.
karten.r: for when the sequence of values is known beforehand; while when only the goal is known.

karten.v: nested
karten.r: If one loop stands in the block of another, the two are called nested.

karten.v: accumulator
karten.r: An accumulator is a name that is bound to a starting value before a loop and combined with the new value in every iteration, for example with summe = summe + wert.

karten.v: break ends a ______ immediately, typically after a find.
karten.r: break ends a loop immediately, typically after a find.

karten.v: continue skips the rest of the current ______; the loop keeps running.
karten.r: continue skips the rest of the current iteration; the loop keeps running.

karten.v: In ______ loops, the inner loop runs all the way through in each iteration of the outer one; break leaves only the inner loop.
karten.r: In nested loops, the inner loop runs all the way through in each iteration of the outer one; break leaves only the inner loop.

karten.v: An ______ starts before the loop with 0 (sum, count) or 1 (product) and takes in one value in every iteration.
karten.r: An accumulator starts before the loop with 0 (sum, count) or 1 (product) and takes in one value in every iteration.

karten.v: The mean is a sum ______ divided by the count; the maximum is an accumulator that is replaced only by a larger value.
karten.r: The mean is a sum accumulator divided by the count; the maximum is an accumulator that is replaced only by a larger value.

karten.v: Guess and check, exhaustive search
karten.r: Guess and check, also called exhaustive search, goes through the possible solutions in a fixed order and checks each one.

karten.v: approximation
karten.r: A number $g$ is an approximation of $\sqrt a$ with the tolerance $\varepsilon>0$ if $|g^2-a|<\varepsilon$.

karten.v: stepping method
karten.r: The simplest method for finding such an approximation is called the stepping method here: you start at $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{g}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0}$ and increase $g$ in fixed steps of step size $h$ until $|g^2-a|<\varepsilon$.

karten.v: ______ is certain to find a solution or to show that there is none, but it needs as many steps as there are candidates.
karten.r: Guess and check is certain to find a solution or to show that there is none, but it needs as many steps as there are candidates.

karten.v: With ______, you do not look for an exact solution but for one that meets a tolerance.
karten.r: With floating-point numbers, you do not look for an exact solution but for one that meets a tolerance.

karten.v: Bisection
karten.r: Bisection repeats the following as long as $\mathit{hi}-\mathit{lo}>\varepsilon$.

karten.v: Theorem 7.3 (Number of steps of bisection)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{n}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\Bigl\lceil\log_2\frac{L}{\varepsilon}\Bigr\rceil}$$

karten.v: In every step, ______ replaces the endpoint that lies on the same side of the zero as the midpoint by the midpoint.
karten.r: In every step, bisection replaces the endpoint that lies on the same side of the zero as the midpoint by the midpoint.

karten.v: With the starting interval $[0,\max(1,a)]$, ______ finds $\sqrt2$ to twelve digits in 41 steps.
karten.r: With the starting interval $[0,\max(1,a)]$, bisection finds $\sqrt2$ to twelve digits in 41 steps.

karten.v: ______ needs $\lceil\log_2(L/\varepsilon)\rceil$ steps; every tenfold increase in accuracy costs only about 3.3 more steps.
karten.r: Bisection needs $\lceil\log_2(L/\varepsilon)\rceil$ steps; every tenfold increase in accuracy costs only about 3.3 more steps.

karten.v: quadratic convergence
karten.r: If $\delta_n$ is about $10^{-p}$, so that $g_n$ has about $p$ significant decimal digits, then $\delta_{n+1}$ is at most about $10^{-2p}/2$: $p$ significant digits become about $2p$. This property is called quadratic convergence.

karten.v: Definition 8.1 (Newton's method)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{g_{n+1}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{g_n-\frac{f(g_n)}{f'(g_n)},}$$

karten.v: Theorem 8.2 (Error of the Newton step for the square root)
karten.r: $$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{d_{n+1}}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{d_n^2}{2g_n}.}$$

karten.v: In every step, ______ jumps to the zero of the tangent line.
karten.r: In every step, Newton's method jumps to the zero of the tangent line.

karten.v: With ______, the error is squared in every step, and the number of significant digits doubles.
karten.r: With Newton's method, the error is squared in every step, and the number of significant digits doubles.

karten.v: Newton needs a nonzero derivative, a starting ______ close to the solution and a suitable tolerance; then it is very fast, otherwise it can cycle, crawl or run forever.
karten.r: Newton needs a nonzero derivative, a starting value close to the solution and a suitable tolerance; then it is very fast, otherwise it can cycle, crawl or run forever.

karten.v: math.sqrt delivers in one call the result that the ______ by hand reach only approximately and with a carefully chosen tolerance.
karten.r: math.sqrt delivers in one call the result that the methods by hand reach only approximately and with a carefully chosen tolerance.

karten.v: ______ reliably finds the monthly interest rate of 0.6183 % in 35 steps.
karten.r: Bisection reliably finds the monthly interest rate of 0.6183 % in 35 steps.

karten.v: Started close to the solution, Newton needs 5 steps; far away, it crawls, because $q$ decreases in every step only by about one $n$-th, and it is then slower than ______.
karten.r: Started close to the solution, Newton needs 5 steps; far away, it crawls, because $q$ decreases in every step only by about one $n$-th, and it is then slower than bisection.

karten.v: The sum in the parentheses
karten.s0:
Let $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{G}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{1+q+q^2+\cdots+q^{n-1}}$. Multiplying by $q$ shifts every term by one place: $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{qG}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{q+q^2+\cdots+q^n}$. In the difference $qG-G$, all terms cancel except $q^n$ and $1$, so $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{(q-1)\,G}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{q^n-1}$, and with $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{q-1}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{r}$

$$\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{G}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{\frac{q^n-1}{r}}$$
$$(r\ne0).$$
s: Substituting this gives $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{S_n}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{Kq^n-R\,(q^n-1)/r}$. From $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{S_n}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{0}$, it follows that $\textcolor{#1b7f4a}{R\,(q^n-1)}\textcolor{#15633a}{=}\textcolor{#c2410c}{K\,r\,q^n}$, and dividing by $q^n-1$ gives the annuity formula; the second fraction results from dividing the numerator and the denominator by $q^n$.
